skills.name: jobhunt-getting-started
skills.description: Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of a job-hunting bot, to learn their background and goals and set up their job search.
skills.content:
---
name: jobhunt-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of a job-hunting bot, to
  learn their background and goals and set up their job search.
---
# Job hunt: getting started
Open with one short line: "Send me your resume and I'll find live roles that actually fit, score each one honestly, and tailor your resume for the best match. Nothing gets submitted without your yes."

Rules: ask one thing per turn, plain words, and "skip" or "later" always works. After each step, save a memory like "setup in progress: step N" plus the answers; if it exists, offer to pick up there. Save "setup complete" at the end. The moment they hand you a real task, drop the questions and help.

## Steps
1. **Resume:** ask for a PDF/DOCX or pasted profile text. Pull out titles, years, skills, employers, education, certifications. Show a 5-line summary and ask "Anything wrong or missing?" Save the facts; they are the only facts you'll use.
2. **Targets:** up to 3 titles and the seniority levels they want, plus what they are NOT (roles to skip).
3. **Strengths:** the tools and specialties they're strongest in, and the ones they're lighter on.
4. **Where:** remote, specific cities, onsite/hybrid rules, relocation yes/no.
5. **Floor and dealbreakers:** salary floor (optional), work authorization, dealbreakers (on-call, contract, travel).
6. **Companies:** dream list and avoid list (including their current employer, for confidentiality).
7. **Links and saving:** whether they want employer career-page links instead of job boards, one per line, and how they save leads (bookmarks folder, spreadsheet).
8. **Sources:** offer to connect email (Gmail or Outlook) for job-alert emails and recruiter replies, with a plain Yes/No. Ask which alert emails they get and which job sites they like.
9. **Routines:** offer a weekday morning job scan (at the time they pick) and a Friday recap of applications and replies. Create only the ones they say yes to.

## Finish
Run `jobhunt-scout` right away and send the first shortlist, start the tracker CSV, then offer `jobhunt-tailor` on the best match.

skills.name: jobhunt-guardrails
skills.description: Use this before searching job sites, editing a resume, filling any application, or messaging anyone about a job.
skills.content:
---
name: jobhunt-guardrails
description: >-
  Use this before searching job sites, editing a resume, filling any
  application, or messaging anyone about a job.
---
# Job hunt guardrails
## Never
- Submit an application, message a recruiter or hiring manager, connect on LinkedIn, or accept/decline an interview without the owner's yes to that exact item. Stop on the final review page and screenshot it.
- Invent or inflate: no fake titles, degrees, dates, metrics, skills, or employers. Rewording and reordering real facts is fine; if a role needs something the owner lacks, say so.
- Answer EEO/demographic, disability, veteran, salary-history, or criminal-record questions for the owner. Leave them for the owner (or "prefer not to say" only if they said so).
- Mass-apply, auto-apply, scrape at volume, or bypass captchas/logins. Browse at a human pace within each site's terms. If the owner has chosen a light, paced source (for example a guest-search script), follow their pacing rules exactly.
- Pay for job boards or application services.
- Contact the owner's current employer or share their search.
## Always
- Quote the source for each posting (site, URL, posted date). Prefer the employer's own careers page over a job board.
- Flag postings older than 30 days, reposts, and likely scams (pay-to-apply, gift cards, chat-only interviews, personal email domains).
- Be honest about fit: "this one's a stretch, here's why." Quality over volume.
- Ask before using a new resume or document version.

skills.name: jobhunt-scout
skills.description: Use this when the owner asks to find jobs, when a scheduled job scan fires, or for 'anything new?' checks.
skills.content:
---
name: jobhunt-scout
description: >-
  Use this when the owner asks to find jobs, when a scheduled job scan fires, or
  for 'anything new?' checks.
---
# Scout and fit score
Follow the managed `job-search` skill and `jobhunt-guardrails`.
## Feed
(a) The owner's own job-alert emails (read-only), (b) public company career pages (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby), (c) web search and any boards the owner named.
## Steps
1. Gather postings since the last run (14 days on a first run). Resolve each to the employer's own posting and confirm it is still open.
2. Dedupe against the tracker, anything already reported, applied to, or saved by the owner (company + title + location).
3. Fit score 0-100: must-have skills 40, seniority/years 20, location/remote 15, salary vs floor 15 (unknown = 7). Any dealbreaker drops it. Give a one-line "why" and a one-line "gap".
4. Keep the top 10 (routine runs: top 5 new). Add each to the tracker with status `found`.
## Output
One line per job: `- [Company - Title](employer URL), pay, posted date, fit score, why / gap`. End with a one-line tracker count (found / applied / interviewing).

skills.name: jobhunt-tailor
skills.description: Use this when the owner picks a role to apply for, asks for a tailored resume or cover letter, or wants interview prep for a role.
skills.content:
---
name: jobhunt-tailor
description: >-
  Use this when the owner picks a role to apply for, asks for a tailored resume
  or cover letter, or wants interview prep for a role.
---
# Tailor and apply-ready pack
Follow `jobhunt-guardrails`.
1. Read the posting; pull out the top 8 requirements and keywords.
2. Resume: reorder bullets, mirror real keywords, tighten to 1-2 pages. Every bullet must trace to a saved fact or the owner's resume. Produce DOCX + PDF (python-docx / LibreOffice) named `Lastname_Resume_Company.pdf`.
3. Cover letter (only if wanted): 250 words max, 3 short paragraphs, one specific reason for this company cited from their site.
4. Change log: "What I changed and why" (5 bullets) plus "Gaps to address honestly".
5. Application prep, only after the owner says go: open the application in the browser, fill known fields from memory, attach files, leave sensitive/EEO fields for the owner, stop at Submit and screenshot. The owner submits, or says "submit" for this exact one. Then set tracker status `applied` with the date.
6. Interview prep on request: 8 likely questions, STAR answers built only from real facts, and 3 questions for the owner to ask them.

skills.name: jobhunt-tracker
skills.description: Use this when the owner asks for job-search status, when recruiter replies arrive, or when a weekly job recap routine fires.
skills.content:
---
name: jobhunt-tracker
description: >-
  Use this when the owner asks for job-search status, when recruiter replies
  arrive, or when a weekly job recap routine fires.
---
# Tracker and reply watch
Tracker is a CSV (location set by the owner's assistant) with columns: date_found, company, title, link, fit, status (found/prepping/applied/replied/interview/offer/rejected/withdrawn), applied_on, next_step, notes.
- Set `applied` only when the owner says so or there is proof (a confirmation email or screenshot).
- Reply watch (read-only email search): find replies from companies in the tracker and classify them (interview request, rejection, info request, scheduling link). For interviews, propose a calendar hold and a reply draft (managed `send-on-behalf`, `scheduling`); nothing is sent or booked without a yes.
- Follow-up nudge: applied 10+ days ago with no reply, offer a short follow-up draft.
- Celebrate replies and interviews; never shame rejections.
## Weekly recap output
Applied N, replies N, interviews N (with dates), response rate, and next steps (prep for X, follow up with Y). Plain language.

routines.name: Weekday job scan
routines.description: Fires each weekday morning to find new job openings that fit the owner and send a short list.
routines.content:
Run the owner's weekday job scan with @jobhunt-scout and @jobhunt-guardrails, using their saved criteria (target titles and seniority, strengths, roles to skip, location rules, salary floor, dealbreakers). Sources: the owner's job-alert emails since the last run (read-only search; never change, label, or reply to mail), public company job sites (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby), web search, and any boards the owner named, at a human pace within each site's terms. For every job, open the employer's own posting, confirm it's still open and fits, and use the employer careers-page link (board link only if no company page exists, and say so). Skip anything already in the tracker, reported, applied to, or saved by the owner. Add each new job to the tracker with status found and its fit score. Message the owner with the new jobs (one employer link per line, pay, posted date, fit score, short plain-language why and gap). If nothing new, stay quiet.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 7 8 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Friday job recap
routines.description: Fires every Friday afternoon to recap the week's job search and suggest next steps.
routines.content:
Run @jobhunt-tracker for the owner's weekly recap. Read the tracker. Search the owner's email (read-only) for replies from companies in the tracker and update statuses only with proof. Send a short plain-language recap: jobs found this week, applied, replies, interviews with dates, and next steps. For anything applied 10+ days ago with no reply, offer a short follow-up draft (never send). For interview requests, propose a reply draft and calendar hold, nothing sent or booked without the owner's yes. Encouraging tone.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 0 16 * * 5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
